To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of glycerol as an additive to a Tris-borate-HPMC entangled solution capillaries for the electrophoretic separation of double-stranded DNA fragments in the size range of 50 bp to 1 kb results in improved resolution and efficiency compared to that obtained without glycerol.

the use of glycerol as a diol component in entangled solution CE with borate buffers results in a marked improvement in separation of double-stranded DNA fragments in the range of less than 100 to approximately 1000 bp.

the addition of glycerole to entangled solutions in Tris-borates improves the separation of small double-stranded DNA fragments in ESCE, and that the mechanism is related to borate-glycerol complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the separation of biopolymers, especially DNA molecules, using capillary electrophoretic techniques.
the development of new methods for fractionating DNA and RNA by CE.
the development of new methods for the fractionation of biological materials by high-performance capillay electrophoresis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of glycerols to entangled solutions of HPMC in Tris-boric acid buffer markedly enhances ESCE separation of double-stranded DNA fragments.
the glycerol-enhanced separation is a result of a combination of the entanglement effect, borate-diol complexation and borate-dna complexation.
the addition of glycerole to a borate-entangled HPMC solution improves the separation of DNA molecules in ESCE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
borate can form 1:2 complexes with both diols and polyols, and the complexes are stable in the pH range 7-10.
glycerol-enhanced ESCE is a simple and robust separation technique that can be used for fractionation of DNA fragments ranging from less than a few hundred bases to about 1 kilobase.
glycerol-enhanced ESCE is a simple, rapid, and sensitive method to separate DNA molecules ranging from about 50 bp to about 2 kb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glycerol, a commonly available and inexpensive reagent, can be used to enhance ESCE performance.
glycerol addition to ESCE buffers is a simple and effective way to improve the resolution of DNA fragments in the 100-1000 bp range.
ESCE performance can be improved by using borate to form entangled solutions.
